sheets.name: README
rows: Traceability view for one regulation-to-SHACL generation run.
Generation is frozen before RDF execution; no ship graph or hidden expected outcome is used here.
events.jsonl is append-only; CSV and Excel sheets are derived views.
Static validation passed and the semantic validator accepted the candidate.
No verified canonical term was available; the generator was not allowed to invent one.
Accepted shapes await the separate bulk evaluator.

sheets.name: RUNS
rows: The candidate is semantically faithful and deterministic validation is valid. It preserves the ship and waterline-case owners, includes the required UIWL input, uses canonical paths and metric-kiloton units, selects the greatest linked case displacement, and applies an inclusive tolerance scaled from the derived expected value without exact-equality logic.

sheets.name: ITERATIONS
rows: Replace the exact decimal equality logic in the maximum-displacement SPARQL constraint. DUI is a derived greatest-case result, so do not require ?equalValue = ?shipValue or reject based on absence of an exact equal case. Compute/select the greatest linked waterlineCaseDisplacement and compare the reported DUI using inclusive bounds with a tolerance scaled from that expected greatest displacement (not from the reported value), while retaining rejection when a case exceeds the reported value beyond the permitted tolerance. Preserve the existing ship/case owners, canonical paths, and metric-kiloton units.

The derived-value comparison and greatest-case selection are otherwise faithful and preserve the required ship/case owners and units, but the SPARQL tolerance uses ABS(?expectedValue). Replace ABS with only the permitted arithmetic (for example, a tolerance based on 1e-6 * ?expectedValue + 1e-9 when the displacement is nonnegative), while retaining inclusive lower/upper bounds scaled from the selected greatest expected displacement.

Add the required ship-owned nltl:upperIceWaterline input (xsd:string, with appropriate presence/cardinality) so the DUI is explicitly tied to the UIWL named by the requirement; the candidate currently omits this declared input despite the retrieved canonical term and requiredInputs UIWL. Retain the existing ship/case owners, canonical paths, metric-kiloton units, greatest-case selection, and inclusive tolerance comparison scaled from the selected expected displacement.

The candidate is semantically faithful and deterministic validation is valid. It preserves the ship and waterline-case owners, includes the required UIWL input, uses canonical paths and metric-kiloton units, selects the greatest linked case displacement, and applies an inclusive tolerance scaled from the derived expected value without exact-equality logic.
